---
title: "Construct a SNP Design Matrix"
---

## Construct a SNP Design Matrix {.unnumbered}


### Description

Build a SNP design matrix from an allele-dosage matrix $X$ (entries
0, 1, 2). Two encodings are supported: VanRaden centering (default,
$W_{ij} = X_{ij} - 2 p_j$) and per-column z-score standardisation
($W_{ij} = (X_{ij} - 2 p_j) / s_j$). The output is suitable for
direct use with <code>run_bayesr</code> and <code>run_bayesa</code>.



### Usage

<pre><code class='language-R'>construct_snp_matrix(
  X,
  encoding = c("vanRaden", "zscore"),
  ref_freq = NULL,
  ref_sd = NULL
)
</code></pre>


### Arguments

<table>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="X">X</code></td>
<td>
Numeric or integer matrix of allele dosages
(typically <code>0</code>, <code>1</code>, or <code>2</code>) with dimensions
<code>n x p_snp</code>. Coerced to <code>double</code> internally.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="encoding">encoding</code></td>
<td>
Either <code>"vanRaden"</code> (default) or <code>"zscore"</code>.
Controls whether columns are additionally divided by their standard
deviation after centering.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="ref_freq">ref_freq</code></td>
<td>
Optional numeric vector of length <code>ncol(X)</code>
giving the reference allele frequencies $p_j$ from the training
set. If <code>NULL</code> (default) frequencies are computed from
<code>X</code> itself (training-set use).
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="ref_sd">ref_sd</code></td>
<td>
Optional numeric vector of length <code>ncol(X)</code> giving
the training-set column standard deviations. Required only when
<code>encoding = "zscore"</code> and <code>X</code> is a test set. If
<code>NULL</code> for a training call, the sd is computed from <code>X</code>.
Ignored when <code>encoding = "vanRaden"</code>.
</td></tr>
</table>


### Details

<strong>Choosing an encoding.</strong>


<ul>
<li> <code>"vanRaden"</code> (default) — centers each column on the
training-set allele frequency. Column variance is proportional to
$2 p_j (1 - p_j)$, so rare variants contribute proportionally
less to the implied genomic relationship matrix. This is the
classical genomic-prediction convention and is consistent with
<code>tcrossprod(W) / k_grm</code> used by GBLUP backends.

</li>
<li> <code>"zscore"</code> — additionally divides each column by its
standard deviation, so every marker contributes equal variance
regardless of MAF. Aligned with alternative biallelic-SNP
parameterisations that assume marker-uniform variance contributions.

</li></ul>

Both encodings work with either <code>marker_type = "multiallelic"</code> or
<code>"snp"</code> in the Bayesian fitters, but <code>"zscore"</code> is intended
to pair with <code>marker_type = "snp"</code> for a fully alternative SNP
convention.

<strong>Training / test workflow.</strong> Always centre (and scale, for
zscore) the test set with <em>training</em> statistics, never with
statistics recomputed from the test set itself:


<ol>
<li> Training: call <code>construct_snp_matrix(X_train,
    encoding = ...)</code>. The returned <code>\$freq</code> and, for zscore,
<code>\$sd</code> hold the training statistics.

</li>
<li> Test: call <code>construct_snp_matrix(X_test, encoding = ...,
    ref_freq = train\$freq, ref_sd = train\$sd)</code> so test columns align
with training columns under the same baseline.

</li></ol>

For phased multi-allelic haplotype data, use
<code>construct_wah_matrix</code> instead.



### Value

A list with elements:


<dl>
<dt><code>W</code></dt><dd>Numeric matrix <code>n x p_snp</code>. For vanRaden:
$W_{ij} = X_{ij} - 2 p_j$. For zscore:
$W_{ij} = (X_{ij} - 2 p_j) / s_j$.
</dd>
<dt><code>freq</code></dt><dd>Numeric vector of length <code>p_snp</code> with the
allele frequencies used for centering.
</dd>
<dt><code>sd</code></dt><dd>Numeric vector of length <code>p_snp</code> with the
column standard deviations used for scaling. Present only when
<code>encoding = "zscore"</code>.
</dd>
<dt><code>n</code>, <code>p</code></dt><dd>Number of individuals and SNPs.
</dd>
</dl>



### See Also

<code>construct_wah_matrix</code>, <code>run_bayesr</code>,
<code>run_bayesa</code>



### Examples
```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, eval=FALSE}
library("masbayes")

d <- load_data("small")
X_train <- d$snp[d$train_idx, ]
X_test  <- d$snp[d$test_idx, ]

# vanRaden (default)
train_v <- construct_snp_matrix(X_train)
test_v  <- construct_snp_matrix(X_test, ref_freq = train_v$freq)

# zscore (alternative SNP convention)
train_z <- construct_snp_matrix(X_train, encoding = "zscore")
test_z  <- construct_snp_matrix(X_test, encoding = "zscore",
                                ref_freq = train_z$freq,
                                ref_sd   = train_z$sd)

stopifnot(ncol(train_z$W) == ncol(test_z$W))




```
